title: Find the Bug: D Flip-flop Reset Polarity
statement: A D flip-flop was intended to have an active-high asynchronous reset, but the provided implementation resets on the wrong polarity. Your task is to write the corrected module. The output q should clear immediately when reset is high. On clock edges with reset low, q should capture d.
module_signature: module fixed_dff(input clk, input reset, input d, output reg q);
behavior: When reset is 1, q becomes 0 immediately.
When reset is 0, q captures d on the rising edge of clk.
q must not update on the falling edge of clk.
The corrected design must not treat reset as active low.
constraints: Do not use delays inside the design.
example:
Broken idea: always @(posedge clk or negedge reset)
Correct behavior:
reset d clk_edge q
1     x no       0
0     1 yes      1
0     0 yes      0
hint: The sensitivity list should use posedge reset, not negedge reset.
